subject: Exact sparse CAR with cheap determinant calculations

messages.author: 4e90fa9f1b035969
messages.subject: Exact sparse CAR with cheap determinant calculations
parts:
Here's a fast and exact sparse conditional autoregressive (CAR) model that extends the sparse approximate approaches provided by Kyle Foreman and others in previous threads.

Source code is here: https://github.com/mbjoseph/CARstan and I've also attached pdf summary of what's going on. The main trick is that the determinant for the multivariate normal prior on the spatial random effects can be computed efficiently following a trick described in Jin, Xiaoping, Bradley P. Carlin, and Sudipto Banerjee. "Generalized hierarchical multivariate CAR models for areal data." Biometrics 61.4 (2005): 950-961.

This determinant trick with the sparse matrix operations that Kyle Foreman developed provides 1-2 order of magnitude speedups with the Scottish lip cancer example. I developed this in the context of a univariate proper CAR model, but the determinant trick also applies to multivariate CAR models.

Here are some previous relevant threads for context:

https://groups.google.com/d/topic/stan-users/he7BxxHfBfk/discussion
https://groups.google.com/d/topic/stan-users/M7T7EIlyhoo/discussion
https://groups.google.com/d/topic/stan-users/x7ud75POybQ/discussion
https://groups.google.com/d/topic/stan-users/iddShgJVwTQ/discussion
https://groups.google.com/d/topic/stan-users/S8dhFpn0Lg8/discussion
https://groups.google.com/d/topic/stan-users/63m5A5ATzs8/discussion

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Exact sparse CAR with cheap determinant calculations
parts:
I posted Max Joseph's rendered case study,

Exact Sparse CAR Models in Stan

This document details sparse exact conditional autoregressive
(CAR) models in Stan as an extension of previous work on approximate
sparse CAR models in Stan. Sparse representations seem to give order
of magnitude efficiency gains, scaling better for large spatial data sets.

here's the direct link:

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies/mbjoseph-CARStan.html

Thanks, Max!

The top-level case studies page with links to all of the case studies
and instructions for contributing your own is here:

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies.html

- Bob
